P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Article 212 of the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 says every natural or legal person may keep all foreign currency they receive, own or hold, and may deal in it or carry out any foreign-currency operation, including transfers into and out of Egypt. Banks may carry out all foreign-currency operations (Art. 214). No mandatory conversion to EGP is stated. CBE leaves foreign-currency cash withdrawal limits to each bank's own policy (21 Aug 2024).

Whether the 2024-2026 FX liberalisation added documentation rules for freelancer inflows was not researched.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can individuals hold a foreign-currency bank account?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Art. 212 gives natural persons the right to keep foreign currency, and Art. 214 lets banks accept foreign-currency deposits and transfers. Foreign-currency cash withdrawal limits are set by each bank (CBE, Aug 2024).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual selling digital products or services register a business? How (sole proprietor), cost, online?
L1_registration.answer: Freelancers and content creators must REGISTER FOR TAX within 30 days of starting (Art. 25, Unified Tax Procedures Law 206/2020), per the Egyptian Tax Authority's statement on content creators (Aug 2026). Registration is at the local tax office or via ETA's e-portal. You need a copy of your national ID, a lease or ownership deed for the place of activity, and a recent utility bill. You receive a tax card and tax registration number. Since 29 July 2026 a temporary tax card valid for 8 months is available, but it can't be used for e-invoices or e-receipts. Whether a freelancer also needs a commercial register entry was NOT established.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax identification number requirement and how to get it
L2_tax_id.answer: A tax registration number on a tax card (البطاقة الضريبية) from the Egyptian Tax Authority. Apply within 30 days of starting activity at the local tax office or via ETA's e-portal, with your national ID copy, proof of premises and a utility bill (L1). Content creators can't deduct payments to other freelancers (e.g. editors) unless the payee's tax registration number appears on the documents (Enterprise, citing an April 2026 ETA warning).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: How residents' foreign-sourced or digital income is taxed
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Income tax under Law 91 of 2005 as amended. The Egyptian Tax Authority states that content-creation income is taxable whether earned in Egypt or abroad, as long as Egypt is the centre of the activity; the same applies to freelancers paid by foreign clients. Small businesses and freelancers with annual turnover up to EGP 20 million may instead opt into Law 6 of 2025's simplified regime (since 1 March 2025): a final tax on turnover of 0.4% (up to EGP 500k), 0.5% (500k-2m), 0.75% (2-3m), 1% (3-10m) or 1.5% (10-20m). The regime does NOT cover professional consultancy businesses earning at least 90% of turnover from one or two clients.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported services and digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT Law 67 of 2016 (ETA English translation, updated 15 Jan 2023): standard rate 14% (since FY 2017/18); registration is required once 12-month sales reach EGP 500,000, BUT exporters must register regardless of turnover (Art. 16). Exported goods and services are zero-rated under conditions in the Executive Regulations (Art. 4 area). ETA's exported-services guideline (Nov 2025) confirms remote B2B services to non-resident business customers are zero-rated with input-VAT refund, and lists bank-transfer proof among the documents. A secondary source (Enterprise) says most freelancers must register for VAT from day one because professional services carry a 10% table tax.

sources.quote: Importer of a taxable commodity or service for the purpose of trading, exporters or distribution agents shall apply to ETA for registration regardless of their transaction volume..

L4_vat_gst.notes: TRAP: 'exporters ... register regardless of their transaction volume', so a freelancer exporting services may need VAT registration even below EGP 500k (zero-rated, but filings are required). The 14% rate is from the 2023-updated translation; PwC notes Law 157 of 2025 amended VAT rates and ETA Instruction 45 of 2025 unified exported-services treatment, neither read. The ETA guideline examples are B2B (company to non-resident business); B2C exports and individual sellers were not covered. The 10% table tax on professional services comes from Enterprise and Fonoa (search summary), not the statute schedule.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law: name, year, in force?, regulator
L5_data_protection.answer: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020. Its Executive Regulations were issued by Ministerial Decree No. 816 of 2025 on 1 November 2025, with a one-year grace period that ends 31 October 2026 (some sources say 1 November 2026), two weeks from today. The regulator is the Personal Data Protection Center (PDPC), which launched its electronic portal for accreditations, licences and permits in October 2026. The law sets up a LICENSING regime: general licences for controllers and processors (usually valid 3 years), plus permits for cross-border transfers and electronic direct marketing. Marketing requires prior consent.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: E-commerce / consumer-protection law relevant to online sales
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Consumer Protection Law No. 181 of 2018, with Executive Regulations published April 2019 and amended by Law 20 of 2024 (amendment not reviewed). It covers distance contracting, including internet sales. Consumers may return or exchange goods within 14 days of receipt without giving reasons and without cost (Art. 17), or within 30 days if defective (Art. 21). Before a distance contract the supplier must disclose its identity: name, address, phone, email, commercial registration number and tax card (Art. 37). Practitioner guidance adds that product information must be in Arabic and prices must include VAT.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving). Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (6) Local official channel: Egyptian law lets every person keep the foreign currency they receive (Law 194/2020 art. 212), and banks offer foreign-currency accounts (P1/P2). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
